text.p: The following is a chronology of events leading to the French government's announcement on Wednesday that it would privatise defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF through a private placement.
February 21, 1996. The government says the Thomson group will be sold and aerospace companies Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation merged in a restructuring of the defence sector.

February 22 - President Jacques Chirac says the Thomson group, comprising TV manufacturer Thomson Multimedia (TMM) and a majority stake in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, will be sold in one piece.
March 28 - Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk says his group is interested in Thomson and may bid.
April 16 - Lagardere group says it will bid for Thomson, merge Thomson-CSF with its Matra business and seek partners for TMM.
May 13 - Lagardere lines up allies British Aerospace plc and Britain's GEC plc as potential investors in Thomson-CSF.
May 15 - Lagardere, South Korea's Daewoo Electronics in talks on possible Thomson bid.
June 12 - Daewoo says it is interested in TMM.
June 20 - Tchuruk tells Alcatel shareholders' meeting that the group will bid for Thomson.
July 1 - Alcatel and Lagardere submit proposals to Thomson chairman Marcel Roulet.
August 4 - French government publishes privatisation decree for Thomson. It plans to keep a golden share to safeguard security interests.
September 16 - Alcatel and Lagardere submit bids for Thomson to French government.

October 16 - French government expresses preference for Lagardere bid, which includes plan to sell TMM to Daewoo after a state recapitalisation. Both Alcatel and Lagardere proposed one-franc price for debt-saddled Thomson.
October 20 - Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin says privatisation procedure may be illegal.
October 21 - Unions at TMM call for labour action to protest against the sale of the company to Daewoo, also for one franc. Criticism of the deal mounts.
October 29 - Prime Minister Alain Juppe calls for public debate on Thomson but defends privatisation plan, citing Thomson's poor finances.
November 11 - European Union begins review of TMM/Daewoo deal.
November 13 - EU starts review of Lagardere/Thomson deal.
November 20 - Thousands of TMM workers demonstate in Paris.
November 21 - Paris magistrate opens inquiry into Lagardere chief Jean-Luc Lagardere based on a complaint by single shareholder disputing the terms of a past merger with Hachette.
November 26 - Alcatel reported to be mulling new Thomson offer in the event the Lagardere deal does not go through.
GEC, Alcatel's partner in GEC Alsthom venture, says it is open to dealing with whichever company acquires Thomson.
December 3 - Alcatel denies talk it would use cash from Framatome, another state company it is seeking to acquire, to fund Thomson acquisition.
December 4 - French government suspends sale of Thomson to Lagardere after Privatisation Commission objects to the terms, particularly the conditions of the TMM sale.
December 11 - Finance ministry says TMM and Thomson-CSF will be sold separately -- Thomson-CSF first, and then TMM following a recapitalisation.
December 19 - Thomson-CSF directors write to Juppe and ask that the sale be carried out through a market flotation.
January 8, 1997 - Aerospatiale says it and Dassault may bid jointly with Alcatel for Thomson-CSF.
January 14 - South Korean president Kim Young-Sam tells French envoy Jean-Claude Paye: "I have come to think the French cannot be trusted."

January 20 - Alcatel files fraud complaint in court in case relating to reports circulating last year of a secret conversation between GEC former and current bosses about their designs on Thomson. Alcatel is reported to believe the talk weakened its chances in the bidding competition.
February 13 - Lagardere says it filed court challenge in December against Privatisation Commission decision.
February 19 - French finance, defence and industry ministries say Thomson-CSF will be privatised through private placement and not public offering.
